title: Robust quant profile validation and adaptive layer rescale
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Build a repeatable pipeline that produces model-specific FP8/INT8 quantization profiles with automated calibration, per-layer anomaly correction, and an independent validation suite for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen variants. Background: Several recent quant rollouts regressed quality on edge inputs due to rare but high-magnitude activation spikes. We need a robust, auditable workflow that: (1) collects detailed per-layer activation histograms and tail statistics, (2) applies targeted layer rescale and temporal masking where spikes cause catastrophic rounding, (3) emits candidate quant profiles and confidence metadata, and (4) validates candidate profiles against a held-out eval set and synthetic spike-in tests. Outcome: Allow automated generation of profiles with pass/fail semantics and safe rollout metadata (expected token-level delta, worst-case prompt failures, and rollback criteria).
updates: 2026-01-25: Ticket created after postmortem for ENG-26742 comparison tests. Scope narrowed to Llama/Mistral/Qwen family variants used in hosted catalog.

2026-01-28: Finished data collection harness that exports per-layer activation histograms and 99.999th percentile tail samples to parquet; storage path: gs://redwood-quant/profiles/ENG-32177/2026-01-28/

2026-01-31: Prototype adaptive layer-rescale algorithm implemented: computes layer-specific scale factor based on robust MAD estimator and limits rescale to 0.5-2.0x to avoid destabilizing numeric ranges.

2026-02-03: Ran A/B calibration on llama-70b-v1 and mistral-8x: FP8 baseline vs FP8+adaptive-rescale. Observed median perplexity delta +0.7% on held-out corpus and 99th-percentile token-LL delta reduced by 35%. Saved artifacts in draft PR.

2026-02-08: Edge-case regression discovered on Qwen-14 where attention-key overflow occurs in layer 32 when rescale >1.8x; added guard to clip rescale when KV-norm > threshold. Test added to synthetic spike suite.

2026-02-12: Validation harness integrated with CI. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2147 (quant profile exporter + validation runner). Planning canary rollout after one more run with extended corpora.
acceptance_criteria: Automated pipeline produces an FP8 and INT8 candidate profile with metadata (per-layer scale factors, histogram snapshots, confidence score)
Validation runner computes pass/fail using both natural eval set and synthetic spike-in tests (must pass both)
Canary rollout metadata generated (expected token-quality delta, worst-case failure examples), and a one-click rollback hook documented
No regression beyond 1% median perplexity on held-out benchmarks for Llama and Mistral families; Qwen must show no more than 2% regressions and pass spike tests
qa_notes: Run validation locally: python -m quant_validation.run --profile gs://.../candidate_fp8_profile.json --eval-set gs://redwood-eval/heldout/2026-01 --spike-suite gs://redwood-tests/spike-ins/2026/; CI step 'quant-validate' will fail the PR if pass/fail is false.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: local validation + CI (green). Stage 2: internal canary 5% traffic on production-internal cluster for 48h with live telemetry events quant.profile.canary.*. Stage 3: progressively increase to 25% for 72h if no alerts. Stage 4: full rollout with emergency rollback flag and automatic fallback to previous int8/fp8 profile. Canary stop criteria documented: >2% user-observed error rate increase, >3% increase in token reject rate, or triggered regression on the worst-case prompt set.
implementation_notes: Key decisions: (1) Use MAD-based rescale to be robust to single outlier traces; (2) Persist raw tail samples (top-1k) for forensic replay instead of only histogram bins; (3) Keep per-layer rescale limited to prevent KV overflow; (4) Produce both FP8 and INT8 candidate variants for workload-specific rollouts. Added telemetry events: quant.profile.generated, quant.profile.validation.pass, quant.profile.validation.fail, quant.profile.canary.alert.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: aggressive rescale can push intermediate tensors into ranges that cause attention instability on Qwen variants. Mitigation: add KV-norm guard and synthetic attention-key spike tests; conservative default rescale cap at 1.6x for Qwen. Risk: calibration dataset not representative. Mitigation: include production-sampled prompts (privacy-scrubbed) and augment with adversarial spike generator.
next_steps: 1) Run extended validation with multi-language corpora and additional Qwen variants (due 2026-02-20). 2) Finalize PR and schedule internal canary (2026-02-25). 3) Coordinate with Console team to display per-profile confidence and rollback buttons (depend on PM-4521).
